ratings.comment: 449 was a challenging course, but it is also one of the most engaging classes I've taken throughout my entire time at college. Professor Terrell provides all the resources to be successful and assigns the topics into meaningful, hands-on projects. Professor Terrell cares for his students & its been a pleasure being in his class. MY GOAT
Amazing prof. Great communicator of information, and super approachable. This class was pretty difficult but definitely manageable if you attend the lectures.

Any class that he teaches is going to be a tough, yet you will learn a lot given his teaching style and care for students. He is the best CECS professor that this school has. This class specifically is incredibly math heavy and requires a lot of demos. The grading is based on CLOs, and you have multiple opportunities to make up missed objectives.

this is literally the goat, if you put effort you'll learn and do pretty well. do NOT slack on the chess project though it takes forever. super nice guy you can tell he's teaching for the love of the game

neal is by far the best prof here. he gives in depth lectures that help you understand concepts better than ever. while this class is tough, it was definitely one of the most interesting by using concepts from other classes to build challenging projects. make sure to touch up on some C# before taking! overall a well structured course to learn SDLC.

Don't let my grade reflect poorly on Professor Neal Terrel's teaching. I failed due to my own lack of discipline, not his ability. He's incredibly passionate about computer science, explains complex topics clearly, and holds high standards. He's like the LeBron James of computer science.

The lectures, HW, and projects prepare you for the exam. Nothing should be surprising if you put in the work. Honestly? I took him last fall and my classes this semester feel so hollow in comparison. It's hard to find a professor here that puts in so much effort and makes the class feel rewarding. Thank god he's teaching 475 next semester

Clear grading criteria and expectations. Everything about him is good except for exams. However, I do notice that his attitude did shift from a nice guy to kind of tired/not very nice. Could be other section/classes weighing down on him. Overall, pretty chill though

This professor is way too hard. His tests are all free-response and insanely difficult. He also expects you do to the project, hw, and study for the tests all in the same week. While attendance is technically optional, he clearly takes it personally if you don't show up.

The professor teaches the material too quickly, leaving us with barely enough time to understand the concepts. Despite this, we're still expected to perform well on exams. It also feels like there is favoritism toward certain students, which adds to the frustration. I dont understand how he got a good review

I don't understand how this professor wants us to study effectively. I put in a lot of effort but still found the tests to be extremely difficult. He allows one notecard for the exams, but it didn't seem to help much. The projects are essentially a more difficult version of the homework.
He teaches the material well but his tests are way too hard. He barely gave us enough time to finish his tests and he takes forever to grade assignments.

Good professors are far and few in between at CSULB, great professors less so. Terrell is a national treasure. Not an easy professor but that is not a bad thing. Clear grading criteria, plenty of opportunities to get the grade you deserve, and makes you want to learn the material of the course. If he teaches a course that you need take his section.

Second course with Neal and he's the goat. Favorite class ever. Lectures are engaging, topics are interesting, grading criteria is very clear and makes it easy to get the grade you want. Can demo homeworks as much as you want and makes learning the material easy. Tests reflect lectures. Semester project fairly easy incorporating all the homeworks
10/10 best prof in the cs department, no complaints, take his class if you want to actually learn while still getting the grade you deserve

This is probably one of the best professors I have taken. Amazing and engaging lectures. The course is on Database Fundamentals, which can be quite dry, but he made it entertaining with his humor and was very good at breaking down the topics. The course was very well balanced in difficulty; hard enough to learn but not too easy to feel disengaged.

Neal is goated. But if you're looking for an easy A, you HAVE to put in the effort. No curving. Required to PASS ALL projects to pass the class. Exams are all straightforward, free response/handwritten coding (no such thing as multiple choice). If you can't pass his exams/projects, you should probably change majors.

One of the best professors in the CS department!! His lectures are super well-taught, and he is really easy to talk to during office hours. Absolutely amazing as a professor and really wants his students to succeed. His exam reviews are 1 to 1 on the exams, please do the readings for his quizzes! Honestly my favorite professor ever! Fair grader!

Awesome professor, super detail in his projects description. Pay attention to the class and put in the work you will do more than amazing. Makes the classes and the lectures very interesting and is able to convey the information in a very respected and very understandable manner. Take him and your gonna have a fun semester.
Man is goat, man is good. Very easy A if you study and ask questions when confused. His tests are straight forward and is basically the same as his guides

Easily the best professor in the comp sci department. Great lectures with slides and recordings on Canvas. Assigned textbook readings aren't required, but is good and help immensely. Grading for projects is very detailed and not too bad, homework graded on participation and shown effort. Study guides mirror exam material and reflect in class topics

Databases is not an easy subject but Terrell does a good job of making sure you understand the topics. The project and exams are straightforward and his office hours make it easy to ask for help if you're struggling. He cares a lot about making sure students learn useful skills that will be applied throughout their CS career.

All around great professor. Presents content in a clear manner, helps with homework and projects as much as he can, and gives you tools to help test-taking during exams. Easily the best professor I've had here.

He was very particular about us knowing real technology to ensure we'll be employable after school. His tests are very well put together. Weeks were given for the 3 projects and only take a weekend. He made the best lectures for very boring material & the class would be very difficult to pass without attending. PraireLearn quizzes are forgiving.

Really great professor! He is very friendly and clearly explains the lecture in an entertaining way. If you miss a lecture, don't worry because he posts the recording, so you could watch it anytime. His exams are a little hard but that is just because they are all written. Other than that, he cares about his students and will teach you well.

Great professor, just databases don't interest me so the lectures can be quite boring. Group projects will save your grade if you don't do well on exams, hw is graded if done, and his exams are pretty hard. He will make you work and learn, but he's super helpful if you ever have any questions. Neal also knows his stuff which is a nice change

What a truly great professor. He has very good slides that we used before any exam or assignment date and he has a very clear way of explaining the material. He is not an easy professor though, you will have to put in the time outside of class (practicing sql/mongodb/uml) to be able to understand the material and do well on his exams.

Exceptional professor. Lectures are interesting and easily digestable. Textbook was free. Answers questions promptly and with great detail. But be prepared to put in outside-class time because the term project is pretty dense. Exams are all free response, use his study guides. If you could handle 328 then this class shouldn't be a problem for you.

Professor is amazing and knows the stuff he is teaching. Makes lectures enjoyable and fun. Only issue with his 342 class are the labs. They are a lot of work and they are not worth a lot. Exams decide your grade in this class. There are very few homeworks so messing up in one can also affect your grade by a lot. Exam index card. Recorded lectures.

Neal is probably the most well liked prof. in the cs dept. His course is difficult but he is extremely accessible and very caring/understanding to students. You must do the hw and study hard for the exams to pass, but in the end you will learn so much. Lectures are fantastic but extremely important when it comes to exam time.

Neal Terrell is by far the best professor I have had here. He is a gem in this gloomy(and pretty terrible) cs department. Neal is an exceptionally strong lecturer and comes in well prepared. CECS 323 is a pretty tough class but Neal will prepare you as best as is possible. Only complaint is that I wish we got more practice on writing queries.

This man is an A+ teacher and he expects as much as he gives. 

I had no trouble getting an A in his class because doing the homework he assigned prepared me for tests. 

He is extremely detail oriented and will dock -0.5% for every miniscule error you make. His assesments are both just and ruthless. 

You will learn a lot, expect to sweat.

The main difficulty comes from the workload and the amount of material covered. Exams are fair if you study the study guides and rubrics are provided for the projects. Weekly reading quizzes focus on logic and application. Make sure to get help or project clarifications from Neal on Campuswire or office hours. Easy to pass class, fair A. No curve.

One of the best professors/lecturers in the university and the best in the CECS department hands down. His lectures are engaging, incredibly informative and educational. He does an incredible job at teaching the subject matter. I've only had the privilege of taking him twice but I would have taken him for more classes had I been given the chance.

Neal is hands down the best professor at this school. I never felt more engaged in any type of learning environment than any class that I have taken before. He engages everyone in the lectures, an offers a lot of help. It was a very difficult class, but there is a ton of material that you are exposed to and they're helpful information. Take Terrel!

Pretty much an easy A if you have taken a Computer Science class before. Make sure you test edge cases on the projects. He often has his grumpy days, but that's because he needs to overlook over 200 students, but he does care for students. Don't overthink projects as most relate to Zybooks or even come back to it.

GOAT teacher. Take Neal if you can. Very effective at teaching and a hilarious guy. Loves joking around with students during lectures. Weekly readings and labs thru zybooks, 3-4 projects, midterm, and final. Projects carry the most weight. VERY specific with grading. Test your project code thoroughly, a single typo could mess your grade up!

Neal is the best professor in the CS department I've had so far, the dude makes you fall in love with comp sci and provides all the resources and help you need. I love his way of teaching, took him for 174 and 277 and will take him again for upper div classes

Neal is a solid choice! Had 3-4 major coding projects and had 2 tests and a final. Clear instructions are given with each project. Very approachable when he has his office hours. Try to sit towards the front and attend lectures because he can give hints regarding tests. Used zybooks for online assignments.

One of the best professors I've had the pleasure of learning from. Extremely good informative lectures. Exams are hard (even online) but Neal makes sure you understand everything if you ask for help. 5 programming assignments, all moderate in difficulty. One of the most caring professors on campus. If you get the opportunity to take him, do it!

Excellent, clear lectures that follow a logical order throughout the semester. You will get a lot out of this class. Tests are hard, but fair. Advice: DON'T TURN IN YOUR LABS LATE!! I did fairly well on labs and tests and ended up with a B because I was always late by a day or two. Don't make my mistake!

He is really good at what he teaches and probably one of the better CECS professors. The class has a lot of reading, homework, and the tests are pretty hard (make sure to read the test questions VERY carefully) especially if you are new at coding. His lectures are kind of boring, I learned more from the interactive book. Make sure to study.
His tests are super hard. Dint take him if you are not good at coding.

This is a hard class but you will learn a lot from it. I made some mistakes and nearly fail, but ended up with a C at the end. Neal is a Nice professor. Just don't cheat or sharing code with your friends. He has 0 tolerance for academic integrity.
Very Hard Class and test are super hard. Won't recommend at all.

Professor Terrell is great and will definitely help you if you ask for it. His exams are tough but that shouldn't stop you from taking him. This past semester there was no mandatory attendance and the textbook is interactive online book from zybooks, which helps understand concepts. You'll definitely pass as long as you put in time and effort

His lectures are very clear. The online book he assigns has mandatory interactive assignments which are actually useful. Labs are fine. Projects are graded much harder though, and you never know what you could lose points for. He will gladly help you if you ask for it. Overall, you will have to work for your grade, but it's well worth it.

Neal taught me almost everything i know about java, his projects were pretty tough but each one taught a very specific method of coding, his tests were hard but he provides very good feedback on assignments and tests. Always willing to help at office hours.

well its been a year since I took him. He cracks jokes a ton. His lectures made me fell in love with CS. He is the gem of the CS Department so, make time for his class. He is a toughie for HW, and Exams. Grades like a toughie. Willing to help students but not giving away awnsers. A past student of Neal's guided me in the right direction! Learn tons

The best professor I've taken at CSULB. The term project is long and hard, and he expects a lot of work out of everyone but it is do-able. He is very reasonable with grading. He does his best to know how everybody is doing on the project, and helps them out if they are stuck (only if they reach out to him).

Terrific! Neal has a great ability to make complex topics easy to understand. Lectures were great and his labs fun. Tests were hard, but he didn't throw you any curve balls. His class really made me fall in love with the intricacies of programming languages. Just base your schedule around his classes. He's a gem of the Computer Science department.

Knowing that I did not have an opportunity to have any coding classes from West, I had to work harder than anyone else in CECS 100 and 174. He is a great wiz for computer sci/eng. If you try using shortcuts, he will know. The lectures were great His lectures were easy, but the labs, hwk, exams, and finals was challenging. You will learn a lot.

Best professor I've ever had so far. The labs and assignments are interesting and challenging enough. He is a tough grader but if you do the job, you'll be rewarded. Also, do not think that you can pass final without studying, that's what I did and it turned my A into a B. Overall, it was very fun having him as my professor, definitely recommend!

We used an online textbook that required you to do participation - it doesn't notify you about upcoming due dates so remember to check on it the day before. He's a really good teacher - able to explain well, very friendly, and wants to see you succeed. A bit of a tough grader with the homework but you can pass ezpz

The projects were difficult, but very helpful. Tests were also very difficult, but will prepare you for the future. Other 328 classes were an easy A, but students leave class without learning anything. This class is very difficult, but you will learn a lot. Glad I chose this professor

Among everyone I've talked to about CECS professors, all agree that you should always take Neal Terrell if you have the option. Not necessarily because he is easy, but because he is extremely effective at teaching while still keeping the class as straight forward as possible. I came out of this class very confident in programming.
Lectures are funny and informative. Workload is fairly modest, and while the tests are difficult he's a not a harsh grader so don't stress too much. Highly recommend.

Neal is an awesome professor, but if you are a slacker like me, you will suffer. He will push you harder than any other professor and make sure you learn. Personally, I couldn't handle this class, I was easily intimated by his intellect and I let it get to me. He's one of the best professors here, but get ready to work.

Great professor and even better that he knows Eric Hernandez another great professor. His lectures are entertaining and great. He seems to be a wizard so don't be fool by his appearance he can cast a big fat F on your test if you don't study. His tests are challenging, but makes you think. Overall he's a wiz and I'll definitely take him again.
His lectures are very detailed and he gives notes so you can follow along easier. Be prepared to work though because this class moves fast.

Excellent professor. No doubt that  you'll walk out the class learning something under his instruction. He's funny and very easy-going. Don't let that fool you; this man will push you and give you a tough time if you slack off! Don't ever be late on quiz days!

Neal is hands down the best professor I have taken so far at CSULB. He is very knowledgeable and understands the material very well. His lecture basically consists of him going through programs, explaining what each line of code does. However, his tests are very challenging and force you to think. Overall, if you want to learn, take his class.

Honestly, hands down one of the best professors I've ever taken. If you're a CS major, try and get Terrell for all of your classes. He makes his class hard so that you actually get something out of the class. There was a lab a week, and each lab built off the other one so don't fall behind. Study for tests ahead because they're hard, but doable.
He is one of the best Professor CECS department has to offer. He actually wanted to teach the students. Would take again.

Neal is amazing, but he is brutal. This class should be avoided if you are a slacker. He explains things very well and makes C++ seem like the coolest language ever. Neal is tough, he expects a lot of work from you and his exams test your knowledge conceptually rather than just implementation of code.  Projects are very demanding as well.

Probably one of my favorite professors in the entire CECS department. I studied hard and made sure all my projects were top quality, and his class was genuinely interesting. Had no C++ experience prior, but felt confident after class was finished. As long as you try and ask questions when you don't understand you'll do well.
Best professor at Long Beach by a mile. If you need help he will work with you. Attend lectures, do the homework, and finish the labs on time. You shouldn't have to worry too much about it.

My favortie professor! He makes every lecture interesting. He knows what he is talking about. The projects are  nightmares and  the test are worse but he is willing to help in anyway possible. If you do not understand do not hesitate to ask, he may look intimidating but he is really nice.  You have to work hard for that passing grade.
Helps a lot. Expects more from his students. Would recommend!

Great professor, and at the start of the semester he lays it out very clear: "I won't trick you on the tests, but they won't be a cake walk." Group assignments are challenging and his tests are mostly based off those. Goes a little fast during lecture but has no problem explaining things in greater detail if you ask. Hope I have him again in 282.
He knows what he is doing and does a better job than other professors in the department.

The best professor on campus for people who actually want to learn. Your worst nightmare if you are a slacker.  You won't pass this class if you procrastinate or miss class often. Each lecture is very dense and a lab after to help you understand. He will gladly help you if you put in effort to the problem.  Relates to students and is hilarious.

I took him for C++ and I was amazed as to how clear and concise his lectures were. He provides notes to his lectures and rarely uses the required textbook. Projects can be long and somewhat difficult if you don't put the effort in. Overall, he is very funny and truly knows his stuff. Take him if you can!
Very clear lectures and helpful with questions. Hard-ish assignments, but not bad. There is some leeway on late work. Little to no text reading.
Very high on my list of best teachers. Easy to talk to, receptive to questions of all levels, and knowledgeable. Will work with you as much as you want to to master the material. Very fair.

Excellent Professor. Clear, funny, and definitely helpful. After finishing multiple lower division CS courses with Neal, I close my eyes at night with only one thought: the avocado. Scoring highest on the exam will grant you the prize jewel. But after multiple exams the thirst for my precious grew until all I ever wanted in life was... the AVOCADO.

Professor Terrell is by far one of the best in the school. Crystal clear lectures. He is very helpful and friendly. He gets so excited about the topic that it MAKES you be interested yourself (228 is usualy not all that fun). He makes abundant corny jokes and nerdy references. Tests are fair, based on the hw mostly. Curves. Highly Recommended!!!
One of the better lecturers in the department. He really understands what he's talking about and is ready to give real world examples to help tie everything together.

best professor i have this semester. His lectures are very clear and he explains in detail. Very chill guy and down to earth. his test is basically from the group assignments and he does curve the test grades. Definitely recommend.

Class is simple and straightforward. Neal provides many examples in his lecture notes. He makes everything easy and clear, and overall just do all the labs and you can get an A. It's an easy A , IF you try/study.

this guy is freakin hot! oh my god have my babies! he can teach java really well and makes the class very fun, if you know what im saying. This is rare because i always fall asleep in class, but how can u fall asleep with such a dreamy face. TAKE HIM!

Discrete Math is a tough subject. However, Terrell makes this subject as painless and fun as possible. I have had him in the past in CECS 174 and I am currently taking CECS 274 with him as well. His style of teaching is clear and concise, and he will never hesitate to lend a helping hand. He has also made me into a much stronger programmer as well.

I am taking 274 with Terrell right now, and he is the best programming professor I've ever had. Everyday you learn something new, and his teaching style is clear and to the point. If you need help, he's there for office hours or will help you in lab. Hopefully he teaches more classes in the future.

One of the best teachers in the Computer Science program. Mr. Terrell is clear, concise, and always prepared. He explains difficult concepts in ways that are relatable to real life. I hope I get the chance to take one of his courses again.

A very great professor. Easily one of my favorites. Very nerdy in a good way. He jokes a lot and it makes the class fun. He posts his lecture notes online and thoroughly explains the code during class. He is always available for help and he really helps a lot. His tests are curved as well. I suggest taking him. I loved it and hope to have him again
No homework just quizzes. He just doesn't seem to care much. His quizzes are made through chatgpt. Easy class but you wont learn much

Choose your teammates wisely: if you're stuck with a bad one, professor will not help you out. Harsh grader, gives unclear guidelines. Communicative when it comes to attendance. Has daily scrums in front of class and demos in groups for sprint review. Okay but not the best if you get stuck with (a) bad teammate(s)

I took him for Senior Project. He's a very easy grader and passionate about student projects. We had daily check-ins, so with a strong team you'll do well. Midterms were easy. Attendance is mandatory, but he's understanding if you miss class due to an emergency.

He switched up so hard. He clearly has no passion for the class, his lectures are boring and speaks with a low, monotonous voice. I learned NOTHING in this class, everyone cheats because he dgaf. His quizzes and exams are on lockdown browser, closed note. It's roughly 30 questions per quiz and 60 on the final. Avoid if you wanna learn SWE practices

This professor was originally rated high because exams were open, but he switched to using LockDown Browser. He literally pulled up ChatGPT and we could see his history asking it to make a quiz based on the slides. Lectures are super boring and he reads off the slides. Your grade is based entirely on quizzes and exams with no other way to boost it.

i took 491A and B with him its practically a free class. Easy midterm in the very beginning of the school year and you present every meeting with your team. One of the easiest senior project classes ever

Tests are no longer open note like the other reviews say and he now makes students use lockdown browser. Your grade depends solely on the tests and final so if you do badly on one, goodluck to you and your grade. Nobody shows up to the lectures because they are extremely boring and he just reads off the slides.

This professor is horrible. Only reason he has good reviews was because everything was open note and book, but now he's implemented respondus for the quizzes and final this semester. Only 5-10 show up after a couple of lectures because they are useless and not worth anyone's time. Doesn't know how to properly put grades in canvas. Don't recommend.
One of the easiest A's you can get. Everything is open note and open internet. He doesn't grade attendance. Not much else to say except that this course does not need that much effort.

Grade is only based on 6 quizzes and the final (same format), which are open everything. Lectures were boring and barely anyone shows up after a few lectures, but he's knowledgeable on the subject and he has experience in the industry so maybe you'll find something interesting.

The only things in the gradebook are quizzes about every 3 weeks and the final exam. His lecture is extremely boring and understands that if students will not pay attention in class that showing up is a waste of time, he had very low attendance for my section. Quizzes were open book, open note, and open lecture slides.

He is a great professor. The course is only graded by the open note quizzes and final. Everything is pretty much stated in the notes so it's pretty hard to not get above an A on the quizzes. Easy class, but you will only learn if you put in the effort and not slack off. However, easy A if you don't attend class either.
Beware the Cockburn... 6 quizzes plus a final. Pretty easy

Murgolo is very experienced in industry and it shows through his lectures. However, besides lectures there's not much more the professor offers when it comes to learning about software development. You're graded only by quizzes and tests which are open book making it a very easy class but not the best class for learning retention.
Quiz were open notes. Final were open notes. No attendance required except sometimes for quizzes. No homework. What more can you ask? He's great! I love this.
BEWARE COCKBURN GANG!!! Those days are unfortunately over :(

It was a very nice, easy, and fun class with this professor! If you want to get an easy A, take the class with this professor. The class is all 6 quizzes and 1 final that you do online, and that is it. You will have a lot of fun when taking it, amazing!
He is a chill professor. All assignments are straightforward.
Grade solely determined by quizzes and a final. Straight from lectures and gives insightful tips for software engineering. Would definitely take again. COCKBURN GANG LETS GO :D
We literally had the best class/discord experience. Take for an eazy A. COCKBURN GANG! LET'S GET IT!
cockburn gang B)

I wish I had learned more in his class The guy does not care about his own class Class average was 95% and his lectures were mostly empty He grades on a curve so you better be willing to do anything to stay with the class average Your grade comes from online quizzes, one midterm and one final exam. Good place to get a good grade, bad place to learn
Amazing professor and I would take the class again but you really have to stay on top of the quizzes! Messing one up can really jeopardize your grade.

Professor Murgolo is a very old school professor, a lot of his slides are a very outdated, but super nice guy. He is very understanding and accommodating to students who need help. A few easy assignments and exams based on his notes. Very stress-free class and you will come out having learned a few new things.

Grading is very clear dependent on a few assignments and a large project. Assignments are very easy and project is super manageable. Professor murgolo is very caring and will help with anything you need. Complete all the work and you will get an A.

Semester project worth 50% of your grade but you're graded as you complete artifacts that are all graded equally (meaning the actual source code is worth 5% of your grade). Has a quiz every 2 weeks that end up being worth 40% of your grade, some were difficult as he likes to throw curveballs. Also has a final that is a subset of the quiz qs.

Build whatever you want even something that already exists is allowed. Only grades on the process of software design, not the actual final product, so if you follow procedures but the product is terrible you still get an A. No more lectures at half the semester. Super chill guy. Does not get involved with your work so you can focus.

dr. murgolo is very relaxed about this class--he trusts your group to be able to organize yourselves and work together as a cohesive unit. he won't breathe down your neck all semester, but he does expect to see progress. hes always at office hours and eager to help you with any technologies you might use in your project.
The best professor that I had in the CS department! He explained everything clearly and he tells you what he expects from you.
Best professor in CS! He explained everything he wants clearly!

Frank is very boring. We started on Chapter 9 so you have to learn the syntax for C++ within the first 2 assignments which require you to comment his code. Test are straightforward but assignments can be kind of difficult. He has no experience with Python and will make lots of connections with Java. Talk to him in lab he will help a lot, trust.
Very good teacher we learned a lot during the class He takes the time to explain all the notions if you don't understand them

Murgolo's lectures and examples are realllyyyy helpful for the assignments given. Not going to lie, lectures are kinda boring but he's a cool guy. Patient and great at explaining the errors in your code. Also helps you write more simple and efficient code. He's a gem for the department as it's difficult to get good professors in this field.

Frank is a very boring professor and starts the class off in chapter 9, skipping all the basics of C++, assignments are very difficult but tests are straightforward. Really gotta earn your grade. Curve is generous
He's alright for people who knows java but for people coming from python with java will be hard since he doesn't know much about python.

Lectures are good and have valuable industry insight, though limited by using a textbook he clearly thinks is filled with fluff. But most of what you actually do is quizzes, and they're terrible. They're just regurgitating what's on the book slides word-for-word (and it's a lot to remember) rather than actually applying any SE concepts you learn.

Fantastic lecturer with loads of work experience who can generally answer any question you have. Labs are often written out almost entirely on the board near the due date, which is nice for your grade but makes them pretty boring. Tests aren't very difficult if you show up to class, nothing you won't expect.

So far, Professor Murgolo has been the clearest and the most professional teacher I've had. I loved it when he said in the beginning of the class that no matter how long you have been in his class, he will never remember your name. If Doctor Murgolo is ever going to teach another class that I am going to need, he will instantly be my number one.

One of the best professors in the CECS department. Tests were heavily based on the lectures. He's crystal clear on what he wants you to study and is very specific on the criteria for labs. Lab assignments can be challenging at times but are do-able in the sense you can put it off til last minute. Repeats lectures sometimes, Murgolos da man.
Clear lectures, occasionally will reteach a lecture. He is a tough grader when it comes to homework assignments. for test, just memorize code from the homework and understand it. Curves grades
Murgolo is a great professor, very helpful, very clear, funny, and is open to teaching anything your interested in computers. Definitely recommend him.

For the 2012 semeseter Dr. Murgolo changed the course from a deeper perspective of software engineering to software architecture course.  Basically 12 quizes, and a final worth 20%. The course is harder because the quizes are very abstract.  Fair class but grades are 30% A's,30%B's and 30%C's. Quiz is out of the slides, be readyto Study Study Study

This was an introductory class, so I was not looking forward to this class, but Dr. Murgolo made the class interesting.  He actually was helpful and made the topic interesting.  He also helped me about my major since he is a CS advisor.  The only bad was that this was 8AM class.
He goes off the powerpoint slide in this class. As long as you go over them, you'll be fine for the quizzes and exams.

Dr. Xu is very nice, friendly and easy to talk to. Lectures are clear and engaging, and I like that the projects are open-ended and flexible.

This is the second time I've taken Hailu Xu in the summer. Friendly guy and super laid back but a very dry lecturer. Challenging but rewarding course. Projects are hands-on and help you really understand how systems work. The professor explains concepts clearly, and cheat sheet is lifesaver for exams. Start assignments early.
Really nice and caring prof. Attendance is random. Exams are tough but fair—if you keep up, it's all doable. Would take again!

very nice professor, but lecturers are lack luster. exams were tough, PAs were easy, attendance was randomly called 5 times so make sure to show up at least to get credit. he wasn't happy with the lack of attendance. for a pretty tough subject in OS he's a solid choice to learn and pass. also flexible for preferred programming languages.

It was alright. Lectures can be boring, takes attendance on random days, can be hard to understand concepts from him, and exams were very difficult this semester. However, the projects and quizzes aren't bad to do. He's a chill professor, but tries to make the course challenging.

I think Professor Xu is a kind professor. His teaching style leaves me confused sometimes. He goes to fast or labels things as "easy" and speeds over it; it gets confusing when he does it often. Very kind professor, but a bit boring. Just reads the slides, which is fine because the exams are based on the slides. Allows half page cheat sheet for all exams. the class is boring. Very hard to pay attention during lecture and the whole time in class you are just looking at slides. Hailu is one of the nicest profs I've had though, allows 1 cheat sheet for the tests and tries his hardest to make the class better for us and not unfair.

He is a great and caring professor. Operating Systems is a dull subject but he makes it bearable and he has slides to read off of and study from. You can tell he cares for his students. I wish he wouldn't make his exams so difficult because they are worth a lot of points and if you aren't a good 'test taker' they can cost a lot. His projects are helpful and reinforce the topics we we're learning in class. Overall OS is a dry subject but he makes it rather fun.

One of the best professors to take OS with. Although OS is kind of boring he makes it manageable. Projects are in Java/C. Tests are doable he gives a page cheat sheet. Funny professor that man was baggin on us in class. You can tell he cares about the students. This man keeps it real.

Hailu is an amazing professor and person who is very understanding, knowledgeable, and flexible. He does assign quite a bit of lab (which are done in groups) and they do require a good deal of research outside of class. His exams are definitely fair and he tries his best to let you know the topics ahead of time.

Prof. Xu is a nice guy and very willing to help. There are four group projects and three exams. The final is not easy. Well, lots of students are cheating so just guess that maybe the reason that exams more and more hard. Following the course and if you did well, you can get it.

I enjoyed the material but disliked how he taught it. His midterms were very doable and straight forward. Labs were fairly hard. All hard work just to end up with a B-

A very caring professor and easily accessible. He is willing to help if you have any questions. The quizzes and projects are pretty fine and not hard to go. The lectures are copied from youtube videos. He's also good at explaining concepts and wastes so much class time that lecture only lasts for at most 40 minutes (out of 75 minutes). I ended up having to watch youtube videos in addition to his lectures because he made simple things so confusing. Easy A but won't learn anything.

OS is pretty dry so the lectures were difficult to follow. He creates example tests and goes over them in class before hand, but the the tests themselves are still fairly difficult. In the beginning, he thought we were smarter than we actually were. He didn't give us enough time on quizzes/ tests and we were unprepared for the 1st proj. if you consider yourself hard working and will study the slides and outside material, this course should be passable. this course is obviously challenging and seems to be weeding out which students are competent and which aren't. good luck future cs majors!

He actually ran the class pretty well considering the pandemic and as one of the newer faculty here. Topics, Exams, and quizzes are HARD, but extra credits are given. He is very approachable and helpful.

The course is tough if you do not have rich experience in programming, the professor assumes that you know how to do coding in Python or Java well. The quizzes and exams are VERY hard, you need to pay lots of attention however the time is limited. The professor is a really nice guy and very caring. You need to work very hard.

This professor is a nice guy, but AWFUL to take. His quizzes hardly have enough time to fully answer all the questions, and the projects are super difficult to decipher. He spent the first two months not listening to student feedback when everyone was clearly struggling. Avoid if possible.

Just don't cheat. Assignments contain ghost prompts that will be implemented into your code if you decide to use AI, and he uses that as a grounds of emailing you and demanding an explanation. DO NOT CHEAT. he is sneaky and hides hidden prompts within text if you're using AI. He doesnt use lockdown so do not be tempted to switch tabs. Use online resources but dont cheat

Great guy, but beware of sharing programming assignments; he will catch on and give you no credit for that assignment. Best prof in cpsc I've had! He makes c++ so easy to understand and also fun! Highly recommend taking him! Really nice professor who tells a lot of jokes and makes class enjoyable. Be aware that attendance checks started this semester—some students say they didn't happen before. Quizzes are simple if you study a little. Overall, I highly recommend this class!

Better than Terrell. All quizzes and exams are taken on Canvas. Responds to emails quickly if you have any questions. Exams are similar to the quizzes! Plenty of extra credit given throughout the semester!

An amazing and very experienced professor. He made me remember why I liked learning CS. The difficulty of the class is about what you should expect from a CS class at this level so put in the effort you think you need. Don't cheat since he is VERY attentive to it. Overall, one of the best CS professors in the entire department. Highly recommended!

His lectures are like having a conversation with a professor. He's pretty chill but takes cheating very seriously. No AI and if you tab out on the quizzes he will send you to his office. Quizzes every other week plus a couple of EC assignments and for attendance. Material posted doesn't really help so being in class will give you info you need.

Solid professor, learned a lot. I highly recommend using a second device when taking his quizzes, he won't hesitate to summon you to office hours if he catches you switching tabs. Him and his TA's actively check the canvas log files to catch cheaters on his canvas quizzes.

6 quizzes,6 PAs,2 Exams and he also gives extra credit at the end. BE VERY CAREFUL when attempting to cheat on canvas quizzes. Great professor, Attend his lecture and make sure take note. 6 assignment and 6 quiz, 1 midterm and final. So make sure do all exam and attend the quiz. His grading is base on point, each exam 100 point, so assignment and quiz matters. He also curve and give a extra credit at the end.

Chill dude, I enjoyed learning C++ from him. Remember a few important things though. Don't tab out on quizzes or exams you will get a -1 and go to the dean. If your code matches on PAs there is a decent chance he will give you a -1. He gave us 5% extra credit.

Solid professor. Provides you all the resources you need and is engaging in his lectures. You do have to show up for quizzes and exams, but going to lectures is optional.

Very fun professor, has 6 coding hw and 6 quizzes. While C++ might be hard at the beginning he is very helpful and open to questions. Midterm and final are based on quizzes so make sure to study those carefully and take your time analyzing each question for tricks.

Learning C++ and Linux might be intimidating to some but luckily Professor Gold teaches it in a way that is fun and makes sense, including giving some real life examples that he has had or real life events that relates to what is being taught. The quizzes can be little tricky so be sure to read the code carefully. And yes, C++ is the best language.

Professor was funny, engaging, interactive, and helpful. Most of his content is during lectures with little powerpoint and other additional links so it's kind of important to show up. Heavy C++ with some difficult projects if not started early. Tests and Quizzes are based on lecture

Great Lectures! They are not off slides, so it sometimes is hard to review so show up to class and take notes. Try to learn the basics of c++ before you start. He says its ok if you don't know in the beginning, but he doesn't really teach the syntax so it's easy to get confused the first few weeks. Exams are heavily based off quizzes!

Graded by PA's, Quizzes, and Exams. PA's are manageable if you get help from TA, tutor, friends. He doesn't post much notes to study for quizzes, so study outside resources, a lot of it, to ace. He's a good prof & lecturer, but isn't always prepared. Must use vim for code and questions on quizzes, but you can code on vscode and output with wsl.

Steve is one of the professors in the CS department who truly stands out. Amazing lectures, great feedback, and programming assignments that allow you to digest the course's content fully. Quizzes were pretty tough as the expectation is for you to dig deeper into the concepts but they prepare you well for the exams!

I recommend learning the basics of C++ before taking this course. Coding assignments and quizzes are based on previous assignments, so make sure you understand how your programs work behind the scenes. No lecture slides, Gold just shows up and starts teaching. Classes felt more like a conversation rather than a lecture, which was cool.
Cool professor but lectures are freestyle which make material hard to understand. Quiz and test are not bad.

Lectures really aren't useful if you already understand C++. There isn't much Linux after the first month either. His quizzes don't really align with the lectures sometimes and the programming assignments can be done quite easily. However, he will dock your grade for any minor mistakes made on those assignments. Super cool guy who cares though.
Definitely a great professor who enjoys teaching his teach very much.

Don't confuse professor Gold for Goldstein. They are the OPPOSITE! Professor Gold's lectures were very informative and helped immensely on each coding project he had provided. Quizzes and exams were a bit difficult for me which is why I got a B, but not once did I study and got the majority of the info from his lectures alone.

Funny guy, chill, and laidback. Class is graded based on 6 projects, 6 quizzes, 2 exams, and a lab section. Projects aren't too difficult, but the last 2 require more time. Quizzes and exams weren't too bad either. Lab is group work. Lectures were actually pretty entertaining, concise, and informative. Overall, great professor, easy A/B

Professor Gold is an amazing and caring guy. He explains concepts so well and is so funny. Apart from some tough quizzes, his projects are nothing too hard and exams aren't bad either. Do well enough and he might even let you skip the final. If you are ever confused don't hesitate to ask questions, he will help!

Professor Gold is very approachable and gives great lectures to follow. His grading criteria sometimes isnt the clearest, but his teachings and enthusiasm makes up for it completely. Highly recommend him for anyone wanting to learn and enjoy in doing so.

His projects are very clear, he explains everything well, and his lectures are engaging. I felt like I was actually learning C++ and having fun. Other CS professors I've had at this school feel like they're actively trying to prevent you from learning but that is not the case here. I would recommend.

He's really good at posting recorded lectures. He's a really nice guy who genuinely wants his students to do good in his class. I really enjoyed his class. I'm taking him again for C++. You'll be totally fine if you do all your assignments on time. His demos for projects are just screenshots of your code output.
Pretty good lecturer and tries his best to answer students' questions. Easy class if you just do your projects on time. Quizzes and exam are really easy too.

Only take Gold for 277 if you're willing to put in the work to learn. He does a good job teaching during the lectures, but for the actual assignments, you are pretty much on your own. If you put in the work needed, you will learn a ton. For the 6 quizzes and 2 tests, there was nothing on them you wouldn't learn just from doing the work assigned.

This was my first c++ class and was fairly easy. Gold is a really good professor and he actually cares about what he's teaching as well as his students. The homework assignments aren't too hard and he pretty much teaches you everything you need to know for them in class. Midterms/Quizzes are mostly easy.
If you don't take Gold for 274 you're actually making the biggest mistake of your life.

Great guy and great professor; quiz after every program, 1 midterm 1 final, study for exams using previous quizzes as your guide bc the questions will likely be the quizzes, can opt out on final if satisfied w/ current grade, in class participation is encouraged. Choose this professor, you'll thank me later.

This class is not that bad until you hit BigInts. BigInts will be the hardest project in the class. Stsrt early. Also, do not take this class with PHYS 152 at the same time. Overall a good professor. The only problem is he does not give notes in the class and his lectures are all based on the lab assignments which he gives.

He crakes jokes 24/7 and encourages students to learn C++ to be the main language! Quizzes are based on the projects, so make sure you do THEM! Blizzard and gaming companies heavily rely on C++! Don't freak out because Master Gold is willing to guide you to understand the concepts at anytime! Can't wait to join the programming team next fall!

Well, this class atm is pretty cool rn. He crakes jokes 24/7 and references real life situations to have students really learn C++ the best way as possible. His quizzes and exams are very difficult and different from the lecture! First two projects were easy but after that, they became harder and harder!

I didn't like his class because i didn't learn much. Took him for 282 thinking he's a good prof based on reviews but it turned out way different. I wouldn't take him again ever. His grading criteria isn't really clear.

He is extremely passionate about what he teaches. Imagine taking a class from a goofy dad in programming with 10/10 teaching skills. The lectures are a blast because of the stories he tells which tie into the lesson. I finished the midterm and final in less than 20 minutes.

Gold is a golden professor. C++ can be tricky, but Gold makes learning the language as easy as possible. No homework, but you'll almost always be working on a project that helps you learn the material. His notes help a lot with the projects up until the last two projects. His tests were similar to the projects and quizzes. Some of the quizzes were way different from his projects. You have to demo your project to him in person before you can turn it in for credit. You can tell he really likes programming. He was available for questions during lab.

Professor Gold is an absolute beast, he rides a motorcycle. I call him Professor Thahab. Lectures are very important to survive the class, but it's not mandatory. I love professor gold! I've had him for 274 and 282 now. Make sure you attend lecture! Although it isn't mandatory, he does go over how to do the projects and other important concepts very well. I loved professor Gold. His quizzes and tests were directly related to the material he taught in class. Pay attention in class, and try to participate - you will learn more. Wonderful professor! Important to go to lectures, he explains projects and quizzes during that time. I love him because when he teaches there's no doubt he actually enjoys the material. Great teacher, lectures are interesting and funny. The projects can look tough at first but he give clear explanations to do them. Quiz are really easy and are the main part of the midterms.

Professor Gold is am amazing professor! His lectures are very  interesting but his bi-weekly projects can be a bit complicated.. He does go over the projects in class though and he is always willing to help.

Prof. Gold was great. His quizzes were sometimes tough but I passed all of them with A or B grades. The cool thing was if you were happy with your grade you could skip the final and he would give you the grade you had.

Gold is a great professor and his lectures are really helpful in understanding the concepts. Quizzes for every program, 1 midterm (easy), 1 final ( easy,review midterm concepts).
He is a good professor. The projects are challenging, but the quizzes are pretty easy. The midterms are same of all the quizzes.

Gold is the most chill professor in the department. Not stuck up or strict, like some teachers can be. If you're interested in the material, you can learn a lot from Gold, because he's always willing to help. Assignments aren't too rigorous, but challenging enough to learn something.

Steve Gold is a great teacher! His lectures are fun: he is very easy going and good at explaining the concepts. Programs are somewhat challenging, but definitely doable. Tests are very easy if you finished the lab assignments. Take him!

Awesome guy, very funny. Projects are reasonable and some fun even fun. He may surprise you with a gift before the final exam. Steve does a fine job in this course. His labs were a little tough, but after searching for examples online and reading the book they were doable. he's one of the BEST!! the way he teaches and how he puts his program assignments together is AWESOME! quizzes n tests are pretty easy. haha laid back fun guy. the only bad side of this class is the content its honestly one of the most boring and forgettable math you can do.
